results: A reusable variable-power reciprocal-product bound gives n^(-a) decay for every 0<=a<1 with an explicit constant 4*(2-a)/(1-a). Optimizing at a=1-1/log(n) proves the SHARP logarithmic-over-index bound for the unweighted Hill kernel, without using a divergent full harmonic lattice as a summable majorant.

On the ENTIRE LITERAL original source circle |z-(pi*n)^2|=n, EVERY free denominator |z-pi^2*k^2| is at least n. The FULL reciprocal lattice sum is summable and at most (8*exp(1)+2)*log(n)/n whenever log(n)>1. BOTH ORIGINAL resonant modes k=+n and k=-n are explicitly retained, with their original reciprocal 1/n contributions.

The ACTUAL raw half-denominator 1/sqrt(|z-pi^2*k^2|) is realized as a square-summable Fourier symbol with EVERY original coefficient retained. Its norm squared is EXACTLY the FULL reciprocal lattice sum and therefore has the sharp (8*exp(1)+2)*log(n)/n bound. No complex square-root branch or reduced-mode substitute is used.

The SAME raw half-denominator is also a bounded Fourier symbol with exact supremum bound 1/sqrt(n) on the ENTIRE source circle. The l2 and l-infinity symbol constructions agree with the SAME original raw coefficients on all source-circle parameters.

The source D_lambda^(-1/2) is CONSTRUCTED on ALL original periodic physical L2 inputs with both actual continuous physical outputs and actual source-normalized L2 outputs. Their original Fourier coefficients are the literal half-denominator products. The uniform-output operator norm squared is at most (8*exp(1)+2)*log(n)/n; the L2 operator norm is at most 1/sqrt(n) with exact constant ONE.

The ACTUAL continuous and L2 half-denominator outputs have EXACTLY the SAME physical L2 class, under the original period-two probability normalization. Thus the continuous-output estimate applies to the same original physical function in the Appendix C.4 factorization. These are the FREE half-denominator factors; no bound for the perturbed S_lambda or for the actual projection difference is claimed yet.
